most_relevant.description: Chapora Fort is located in North Goa. There are about 120-150 steps to climb up on top of the fort, not much of trekking is involved. The famous bollywood movie 'Dil Chata Hai' was shot here in this location, many re-create that scene from the movie while visiting this fort. Some also refer to it as the Dil Chata Hai Fort. The view of Vagator Beach from the top is fantastic, it's very relaxing and a good place to sit and experience calmness. It's a good place to visit with friends, while you're in Goa. Good place to visit before sunset, I would definitely recommend visiting this place. There's no entry fee charged.

Chapora Fort is more than just a crumbling landmark—it’s an experience. Whether you're a photography enthusiast, a history buff, or just looking for a peaceful spot to catch an epic Goan sunset with a cool breeze in your hair, this historic hilltop is well worth the sweat.

​Once you make it through the arched gateway and step onto the sprawling grounds, the climb is instantly worth it.

​The Scenery: You are greeted by a breathtaking 360-degree view. On one side, you can gaze down at the golden curves of Vagator Beach and Ozran Beach; on the other, the Chapora River meets the vast expanse of the Arabian Sea.

​The Sunset: Staying for the golden hour is the highlight of the trip. Watching the sun dip straight into the sea while painting the sky in shades of orange and violet is magical.

The best View as to watch sunset 🌇. Come here around 4.30 PM before 5.30 because entry is prohibited🛑 and then track the fort of around 1km and then find a proper wall to seat and watch the sunset.

From here you can see the greenery and Sea ⛵ Vagator Beach clearly. Just spend good time here and enjoy the view and calmness.

Please ensure to take water or snacks with you from parking because there is nothing available.

Chapora Fort also well known by the name Dil Chahta Hai Fort 🏰 this is the place where one of the most famous scene of the movie is filmed 📷.

The fort 🏰 is not the fort 🏰 anymore, nothing much is left though the repair part of the same is started as per the last visit there was lots of brick 🧱 and cements etc. The fort is around 500meter walk from the parking 🅿️ area, also you will get a lot of shops while reaching to top 🔝. However, the price 🤑 will keep on increasing of all the stuff as and when you start reaching the top gradually.

The view 🪟 is beautiful 😍 from the top but there is nothing to do. It's not worth going during summer 🌞 or peak sun ☀️ time as it's very hot 🔥 and there is nothing to take shed of. I don't remember exactly whether there was ticket 🎫 or something.

But yes, overall it's a one time visit thing or I can also say it's avoidable as there is nothing to do.
